causal-factors.name: CDU polling lead / near-lead over Greens in late Feb 2026
causal-factors.rationale: Multiple polls around February 25–26, 2026 place CDU around 28–29% and Greens around 23–27%, which strengthens CDU's position relative to the anchor.

causal-factors.name: Greens closing the gap / momentum gaining for Greens
causal-factors.rationale: Several polls show Greens within a few points of CDU or narrowing the gap (e.g., Greens 27% vs CDU 28%), reducing CDU's lead and raising Greens' chances to win the most seats.

causal-factors.name: sizable AfD share (around 18–20%) affecting vote distribution
causal-factors.rationale: AfD's double-digit support can siphon votes from CDU or alter coalition dynamics, complicating CDU's path to the most seats.

causal-factors.name: Prediction markets / seat projections favoring CDU (~36–37 seats)
causal-factors.rationale: Forecasts and polls translating into seat projections often place CDU ahead or close to Greens, supporting the CDU-leading outcome.

causal-factors.name: Historical swings: Greens have led or topped in 2016 and 2021
causal-factors.rationale: Past cycles show Greens can become the largest party, introducing nontrivial risk to a CDU-dominant seat outcome.

causal-factors.name: Late-deciding voters tilt toward Greens
causal-factors.rationale: Escalating Greens momentum in late polls suggests some undecided voters may favor Greens as voting nears.

causal-factors.name: Greens gain traction in urban/youth demographics
causal-factors.rationale: Urban areas and younger voters in Baden-Württemberg are pivotal; fresh Greens momentum could widen Greens' seat share at CDU's expense.

causal-factors.name: Economic or local governance developments favor CDU
causal-factors.rationale: If economic conditions improve or perceived CDU governance stabilizes, CDU vote share could firm and reinforce its lead.

causal-factors.name: Poll-to-seat translation uncertainty
causal-factors.rationale: Methodological differences and regional weighting create uncertainty in translating poll shares into seats, possibly eroding CDU's apparent lead.

causal-factors.name: Historical precedent — Greens won largest seats in 2016/2021
causal-factors.rationale: Past cycles show that even if CDU leads in polls, Greens have won the most seats in other elections, signaling nontrivial downside risk to a CDU-led outcome.

causal-factors.name: AfD vote share risk (siphoning effects)
causal-factors.rationale: A relatively high AfD share could siphon votes from either CDU or Greens depending on turnout dynamics, with uncertain net effect.

causal-factors.name: CDU polling lead stability in late-February 2026 polls
causal-factors.rationale: Multiple late-February polls show CDU leading or near the Greens, which supports a higher probability of CDU having the most seats.

causal-factors.name: Greens closing the gap in several polls
causal-factors.rationale: Greens narrowing the gap reduces CDU's expected seat lead and increases the risk that Greens could win the most seats if the trend continues.

causal-factors.name: Sizable AfD vote share in some polls
causal-factors.rationale: A nontrivial AfD share can siphon votes from CDU and other center-right options, potentially diminishing CDU's seat count.

causal-factors.name: turnout dynamics favoring Greens in urban areas
causal-factors.rationale: Higher turnout in urban cores, where Greens perform well, could erode CDU's margin and improve Greens' chances of obtaining the most seats.

synthesis: Objections reveal a genuine blind spot around Greens momentum and seat translation, warranting a modest downward adjustment from the ensemble. The final probability reflects both the prevailing CDU lead in late-Feb polls and substantial uncertainty about seat allocation.
